Hi @zooba, thanks for the review! I think you are right, keeping the last assigned value is more suitable.

I added a new reversed loop, to de-duplicated the keys and keep the last assigned key. Overwrite it to the `result` dict in the origin loop is not a good solution, since we must pop the old key and value from the `result` dict.

I'd break this up even more; for example the sorting of `keys` (in `normalize_environment_keys`) is an isolated action that can be extracted as a separate function. Also, you are leaking the result from the `sort` vectorcall; even if you are not using the result, you still need to decref it.

> I'd break this up even more; for example the sorting of `keys` (in `normalize_environment_keys`) is an isolated action that can be extracted as a separate function. Also, you are leaking the result from the `sort` vectorcall; even if you are not using the result, you still need to decref it.

Thank you for your review. I have broken up the old `normalize_environment_keys` into `sort_environment_keys` and `dedup_environment_keys`. The result of vectorcall is also `decref`ed.

Some codes which doing environment key validation is originally in the `getenvironment` function. In the early commits I moved them to `normalize_environment` function because I think it's more suitable.

After reviews the `normalize_environment` function has been broken up into multiple function, so I moved them back, which I think is more suitable now.

The `Assertion failed: (_osfile(fh) & FOPEN)` is likely to be a warning and is not related to this PR.

> The `Assertion failed: (_osfile(fh) & FOPEN)` is likely to be a warning and is not related to this PR.

Yeah, this is unavoidable because our tests try to use invalid descriptors. Normally, the CRT will abort (because it's a coding error, not an "expected" runtime error), but we disable that and turn it into an exception. In a debug build, we can't suppress the assert message (easily enough to be worth it).

I'll take a look at the refactored code when I get a chance, but it sounds like a good improvement overall, so if the tests are happy then I'm probably going to be happy. Don't wait too long for my approval

GitHub fields: ```python assignee = None closed_at = None created_at = labels = ['type-bug', '3.9', '3.10', '3.11', 'extension-modules', 'OS-windows'] title = '[Windows] correctly sort and remove duplicates in _winapi getenvironment()' updated_at = user = 'https://github.com/eryksun' ``` bugs.python.org fields: ```python activity = actor = 'eryksun' assignee = 'none' closed = False closed_date = None closer = None components = ['Extension Modules', 'Windows'] creation = creator = 'eryksun' dependencies = [] files = [] hgrepos = [] issue_num = 43702 keywords = [] message_count = 3.0 messages = ['390038', '415560', '415563'] nosy_count = 6.0 nosy_names = ['paul.moore', 'tim.golden', 'zach.ware', 'eryksun', 'steve.dower', 'asaka'] pr_nums = [] priority = 'normal' resolution = None stage = 'needs patch' status = 'open' superseder = None type = 'behavior' url = 'https://bugs.python.org/issue43702' versions = ['Python 3.9', 'Python 3.10', 'Python 3.11'] ```

### Linked PRs * gh-102731 * gh-113865 * gh-113866 * gh-113867
comments:
The [`getenvironment()`](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/b400219df5f245ef2eb3c7ce0589b1f8020a1192/Modules/_winapi.c#L783) function in "Modules/_winapi.c" needs to sort variables in the environment block and remove duplicates case insensitively[^1]. 

The sort order used to matter with `SetEnvironmentVairableW()`. As soon as it reached a name in the environment block that compared greater than the target name, it would insert a new variable. Nowadays, `SetEnvironmentVairableW()` searches the entire environment block before inserting a new value. Regardless, at the very least, `getenvironment()` is not well-behaved and is not setting the environment in the documented sort order that users, and possibly other programs, expect.

Case-insensitive sorting in Windows uses upper case. The variable names in the mapping can be added to a list and sorted with a key function that's based on [`LCMapStringEx()`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winnls/nf-winnls-lcmapstringex), with the flag `LCMAP_UPPERCASE`. Loop over the sorted list to create the environment block. Remove duplicates by skipping a name that compares equal to the previously stored name according to [`CompareStringOrdinal()`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/stringapiset/nf-stringapiset-comparestringordinal).

[^1]: [Changing Environment Variables](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/changing-environment-variables)
I have a question, how to determine which name should be stored if they are duplicated with case insensitive?

> which name should be stored if they are duplicated with case insensitive?

Ideally `os.environ` would preserve the original case of the process environment, and `os.environ.copy()` would return a copy that's also case insensitive. That would prevent most problems with duplicates keys. See [msg387676](https://bugs.python.org/msg387676) in bpo-28824, and [msg414319](https://bugs.python.org/msg414319) in bpo-15373.

In [msg390038](https://bugs.python.org/msg390038) I suggested keeping the first key that's encountered. However, dicts preserve insertion order nowadays, so one could assume that the last one is the one that the caller wants to keep.

This issue can be reproduced on [msys2](https://www.msys2.org/) (also cygwin, I think) easily:

``` python
msys2 shell $ ABC=1 abc=2 python
Python 3.11.0b1 (main, May  7 2022, 22:58:47) [MSC v.1931 64 bit (AMD64)] on win32
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information.
>>> import os
>>> print(os.environ["ABC"], os.environ["abc"])
2 2
>>> import subprocess
>>> subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", "echo $ABC $abc"])
1 2
CompletedProcess(args=['bash', '-c', 'echo $ABC $abc'], returncode=0)
>>> 
>>> os.environ["abc"] = "3"
>>> print(os.environ["ABC"], os.environ["abc"])
3 3
>>> subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", "echo $ABC $abc"])
3 2
CompletedProcess(args=['bash', '-c', 'echo $ABC $abc'], returncode=0)
```

``` cmd
msys2 shell $ ABC=1 abc=2 cmd
cmd > echo %ABC% %abc%
1 1
cmd > bash -c "echo $ABC $abc"
1 2
cmd > set abc=3
cmd > echo %ABC% %abc%
3 3
cmd > bash -c "echo $ABC $abc"
3 2
```

``` powershell
msys2 shell $ ABC=1 abc=2 powershell
PS > echo $Env:ABC $Env:abc
1
1
PS > bash -c "echo $ABC $abc"
1 2
PS > $Env:abc = 3
PS > echo $Env:ABC $Env:abc
3
3
PS > bash -c 'echo $ABC $abc'
3 2
```

Python behaves differently from both cmd.exe and powershell.

Case-sensitive environment variables are in `nt.environ`, but they don't affect the real environment:

``` python
msys2 shell $ ABC=1 abc=2 python
Python 3.11.0b1 (main, May  7 2022, 22:58:47) [MSC v.1931 64 bit (AMD64)] on win32
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information.
>>> import nt, os
>>> print(nt.environ["ABC"], nt.environ["abc"])
1 2
>>> print(os.environ["ABC"], os.environ["abc"])
2 2
```

This is because environment vairiables are not sorted correctly in `os._convertenviron`:

https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.11.0b1/Lib/os.py#L750

Related to GH-91018, GH-73010.
